name: 3R Nighttime Dehazing Benchmark
description: Increasing the visibility of nighttime hazy images is challenging because of uneven illumination from active artificial light sources and haze absorbing/scattering. The absence of large-scale benchmark datasets hampers progress in this area. To address this issue, we propose a novel synthetic method called 3R to simulate nighttime hazy images from daytime clear images, which first reconstructs the scene geometry, then simulates the light rays and object reflectance, and finally renders the haze effects. Based on it, we generate realistic nighttime hazy images by sampling real-world light colors from a prior empirical distribution. Experiments on the synthetic benchmark show that the degrading factors jointly reduce the image quality. To address this issue, we propose an optimal-scale maximum reflectance prior to disentangle the color correction from haze removal and address them sequentially. Besides, we also devise a simple but effective learning-based baseline which has an encoder-decoder structure based on the MobileNet-v2 backbone. Experiment results demonstrate their superiority over state-of-the-art methods in terms of both image quality and runtime. Both the dataset and source code will be available at https://github.com/chaimi2013/3R.
evaluation_method: PSNR / SSIM (plus perceptual metrics such as LPIPS) and runtime (efficiency)
typical_sota_score: 18–28 dB (PSNR) on the provided synthetic splits
reputation: A specialized benchmark in nighttime dehazing that contributed a synthetic generation pipeline (3R) and has been cited in low-light/dehazing research but remains niche compared to large general restoration datasets.
notes: Synthetic-to-real domain gap: images are synthetically generated using the 3R pipeline which may limit real-world generalization; dataset size is moderate; non-LLM benchmark focused on computer vision; reported metrics include both fidelity (PSNR/SSIM) and perceptual scores.
